text:
Sam (CS): @Maria FYI Acme reported their quantized endpoint (int8-calib-v3) latency spiked after last night's rollout. p95 jumped and throughput dropped. Need urgent help.
Ajay (AcmeMed): Confirming. FP16 p95 ~75ms, int8-calib-v3 p95 ~220ms under our steady load. We flipped the model to int8 at 02:14 UTC. Session 8f7c9d.
Maria (eng-runtime): Ouch. Can you DM me a small repro payload and confirm whether their requests use sticky sessions / KV cache warm?
Ajay (AcmeMed): Sent DM with sample. They have session stickiness on. Not sure about cache warm state.
Sam (CS): They ran 500 short prompts and saw consistent slowdown.
Maria (eng-runtime): Initial hypothesis: calibration introduces extra per-seq ops and may change kernel routing heuristics, plus a KV key layout shift could yield more cache misses. Need traces.
perfbot: Profile for session 8f7c9d available. Highlights:
- kernel_switch_count: 58 (int8-calib-v3)
- kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.57
- avg_batch_size: 2.1
- tail_slow_kernel_latency: 195ms (fallback matmul path)
deploy-bot: rollout int8-calib-v3 -> 100% at 2026-03-17T02:14:07Z
Maria (eng-runtime): High kernel switches + >50% kv miss rate explains p95. Small batches + short sequences push execution into a slow int8 fallback. Also calibration postprocess can reorder KV indices.
Leo (oncall): Repro steps I ran (local canary):
```
redwood perf run --model rwinf/llama2-13b-qcalib-v3 --payload short_prompts.json --count 500 --concurrency 6
perf analyze --session 8f7c9d --summary
```
Result: ~2.5x p95 vs fp16 baseline.
Maria (eng-runtime): Short-term options:
- Route Acme to fp16 variant (fast rollback)
- Apply heuristic: bypass calibration for customers with avg_batch_size < 4
- Patch KV mapping to preserve previous hot-key layout (risky)
Sam (CS): Ajay, do you want us to route you back to FP16 while we investigate?
Ajay (AcmeMed): Yes please, route back to FP16. Stability > cost for now.
Maria (eng-runtime): I'll create canary rollback: rollback-int8-acmemed-2001. Plan: route 100% of Acme traffic to rwinf/llama2-13b-fp16. ETA ~8min.
deploy-bot: Routing change deployed: AcmeMed -> rwinf/llama2-13b-fp16 (canary rollback-int8-acmemed-2001) at 1912349805
Sam (CS): Notified customer: "Routed traffic to FP16 to restore latency. Engineering investigating." They acknowledged.
Maria (eng-runtime): Action items for eng-runtime/infra:
1) Capture full kernel trace under Acme traffic pattern (short sequences, sticky sessions) — Leo
2) Re-run calibration locally with batch sizes 1..4 to measure per-seq overhead — Maria
3) Inspect KV cache key mapping and eviction behavior after calibration deploy — infra team
4) If repro confirmed, add routing heuristic: prefer fp16 when avg_batch_size < 4 for that customer
Leo (oncall): Kernel trace captured: trace-id kernel-2001-01 (artifact uploaded). Preliminary shows attention kernel routing to a scalarized int8 matmul on short seqs.
perfbot: New artifact: trace-kernel-2001-01 (18MB). Early analysis: heavy number of kernel transitions around seq len 16-24.
Maria (eng-runtime): If fallback kernel is unavoidable, we can skip calibration for tiny-batch customers as a quick reversible mitigation. Low risk and we can roll later.
Sam (CS): Keeping Acme on FP16. I'll send daily status updates until RCA items closed.
Ajay (AcmeMed): Thanks for quick mitigation. Please share timeline for RCA.
Maria (eng-runtime): Aiming for initial RCA EOD tomorrow. Owners: Maria, Leo, Sam. cc: eng-runtime, eng-infra. @perfbot please run targeted benchmarks comparing int8-calib-v3 vs fp16 for batch sizes [1,2,4,8] and seq lengths [8,32,64].
perfbot: Benchmark queued, results will be posted in this thread.
Sam (CS): Closing this thread for now — will reopen if customer reports any regressions after the routing change.
